## arc_1064 — Continuation / positive-skew shape family (the one untested LENS, council thread 1063b)

**Disposition: KILL** (obs cheap-kill, §5d). Full record: `discovery/arcs/arc_1064_continuation_positive_skew.md`.
Executes arc-1063's logged-forward thread (b): the corpus tested ONLY reversion shapes, judged by +1R
CAPTURE; a continuation edge survives take-the-loss differently (needs positive SKEW under a runner exit,
not >0.50 capture). Both honest-era lenses (capture; fixed-horizon mean drift) structurally penalize a
positive-skew continuation, so such entries were cheap-killed at the capture stage (arc 1062 the exact
case) before their runner expectancy was ever measured. This arc takes the textbook trend-CONTINUATION
entry (fresh Donchian-N break inside an established SMA50/200 trend, BOTH directions, H4 USD majors) and
judges it by the SKEW-appropriate lens: the long-horizon fwd-return DISTRIBUTION with a pre-registered
guard (G1 mean>0; G2 tail-removed[drop top5%]>0 + per-fold-median>0 majority; G3 per-pair distributed).

**Result (6 cells, IS 2010-2020):** capture ≈0.477–0.488 ≡ unconditional base (the trend filter buys
nothing on +1R capture — closed-ground confirmation). Positive skew is REAL but only at long runner
horizons (drift120 skew +0.46/+0.42, frac>2ATR ~0.38 — winners do run), so thread (b)'s premise is
confirmed at the distribution level. BUT the guard fails decisively in EVERY cell: median drift NEGATIVE
everywhere (−0.11..−0.44); tail-removed mean STRONGLY NEGATIVE everywhere (−0.59..−1.14) — the only
positive mean (D20 drift120 +0.114) is entirely the top-5% jackpot tail; per-fold median>0 only 3–5/11;
binding 2015 & 2018 NEGATIVE in every cell. fwd_drift is GROSS (ignores take-the-loss) → the honest
SL-first engine is strictly worse, so no engine spent; §5f does not bite (the lone G1-passing cell passes
only via the top-5% tail G2 disqualifies).

**Meaning / NEW lesson:** a positive-skew CONTINUATION edge on liquid FX majors is a thin-tail mirage —
the apparent positive mean is undistributed jackpot variance (top-5% carry), the median trade loses, and
the binding folds are negative. The capture-lens cheap-kill of continuation was CORRECT: capture and
expectancy+guard lenses AGREE. This CLOSES arc-1063's last open SHAPE-family lens-gap and REMOVES the
"maybe the capture lens was wrong for skew edges" caveat from the frontier-exhausted reframe — confirming
arc-2000's "fat tail generic, not trend-selected" on the explicit skew axis. Reusable guard for any future
skew/continuation candidate: require per-fold median>0 AND tail-removed-expectancy>0 before believing a
positive mean (a +mean alone on a skewed distribution is the jackpot tell, not an edge).

**Handoff:** Components UNCHANGED (all 4 PORTFOLIO; me_long-solo the honest deploy object). Within-charter
terminus now holds on BOTH lenses (reversion shapes via capture; continuation/positive-skew via
expectancy+guard). Lever = operator path-A gate-governance call and/or charter unlock (M macro / O options,
`NEEDS_ENABLEMENT.md`). Remaining un-executed 1063 thread: (a) the USD-factor correlation-vs-sign crux
(cheap panel query). No BUILT tool registered (single-use driver, pure `observe_long_capture` + a causal
trend-continuation mask + `scipy.stats.skew` + inline guard); no canonical change; no FLAG; OOS untouched.
Driver `discovery/_disco1_work/arc1064_continuation_positive_skew.py`.

## arc_1065 — lens-A: the CORRELATION-vs-SIGN crux of me_long's strong-USD losses

**Chat 1000s. Full record:** [`arcs/arc_1065_melong_factor_vs_sign.md`](arcs/arc_1065_melong_factor_vs_sign.md).
Disposition **KILL** (obs cheap-kill §5d; no new component; me_long UNCHANGED PORTFOLIO). No
engine/null/council; no canonical change; no FLAG; OOS untouched.

**Why this arc (the last open thread).** Resumed the 1000s loop at 1064→1065 (`STOP` absent). arc 1063
(judge power audit) logged TWO un-executed council forward threads; thread (b) continuation/positive-skew
= closed by arc 1064 (KILL). Thread (a) — the USD-factor correlation-vs-sign crux — was the single
remaining logged-not-executed thread in my range. The 1063 council CHALLENGED its own lens-A premise
(*"2015/2018 is a SIGN conflict, not co-located noise → a symmetric veto can't make a year prefer the leg
it rejects"*); this arc settles it empirically.

**The question + why distinct.** Is me_long's strong-USD-block (2014-16) loss a hedgeable
COMMON-USD-FACTOR component — then a beta-sized USD-basket short (shorts now open, PR #273) could strip
it and lift the worst fold — or an irreducible IDIOSYNCRATIC-to-the-regime / sign-conflict effect — then
no symmetric factor hedge helps? DISTINCT from the two nearest priors: arc 1059 (USD-breadth **FILTER** —
conditions ENTRY, drops fires, removes the +2018 directional-WMR help) and arc 2018 (**fully USD-neutral**
cross-sectional — neutralizes the whole common move). lens-A keeps ALL fires and subtracts only the
**beta-sized** common-factor exposure (a HEDGE, the least-aggressive that could still strip the regime
risk while preserving each pair's full idiosyncratic reversion).

**Method.** Obs cheap-kill, gross, no engine. Reused arc-1059 `build_common_usd_move` (canonical
`_month_end_into_move`) + BUILT `observe_long_capture`. me_long committed config (threshold_atr=1.0,
into_bars=2, D1, 7 USD majors), IS 2010-2020, n=126 fires. Per fire: 2-bar reversion `fwd_drift_atr`,
the month's common-USD factor `f`, position USD exposure `+USD_FACTOR[p]`, `factor_signal=USD_FACTOR[p]·f`.
Pooled regression `drift ~ alpha + beta·factor_signal`; within-month sign concordance per year; per-year
RAW vs de-factored (hedged) alpha `y − beta·factor_signal`. Sign-convention-invariant (verified by
re-running both conventions: beta flips, R²/fitted-component/hedged residual identical). Driver
`discovery/_disco1_work/arc1065_melong_factor_vs_sign.py`.

**Results (decisive — the hedge is INERT).** (1) me_long's per-fire reversion outcome has **essentially
ZERO common-USD-factor loading: beta +0.026, R² 0.0003, corr +0.019.** (2) De-factored (hedged) alpha ≈
raw everywhere: mean +0.165 vs +0.147, worst-yr −0.227 vs −0.237, **same 3/11 negative years**; the
**2014-16 block RAW −0.0155 → HEDGED +0.0003 ≈ 0** (2016 robustly −0.23 hedged). The beta-sized USD-basket
hedge removes nothing because there is nothing factor-shaped to remove. (3) **Within-month sign
concordance is HIGH (~0.72)** — held majors fail TOGETHER within a month-end — **but ORTHOGONAL to the USD
factor (R²≈0): the co-movement is the month-end-reversion-works-or-fails REGIME, not a USD-directional
drift a symmetric short could neutralize.**

**Read / verdict.** lens-A CLOSES — KILL. me_long's strong-USD loss is NOT a hedgeable common-USD factor;
it is idiosyncratic to the month-end-reversion regime (the reversion genuinely fails when the down-move

verdict.

**NEW lesson.** A thin reversion edge's per-year fold COHERENCE (here ~0.72 within-month outcome-sign
concordance — held positions fail together) can be **REGIME co-movement, not FACTOR co-movement** — and is
therefore **un-hedgeable by a symmetric directional (USD-basket) overlay** (R²≈0). You cannot strip the
strong-USD loss with a factor short because the loss is not a directional factor exposure; it is the
month-end-reversion-fails-in-a-trend regime itself. Generalizes arc 1059's "edge & tail are the same
exposure" from the **filter axis** to the **hedge axis**: neither filtering systematic entries (1059) nor
hedging the common factor (this arc) lifts the worst fold, because the edge-carrying exposure IS the
non-directional reversion regime. Before reaching for a factor hedge to rescue a thin book's worst fold,
regress its per-trade outcomes on the candidate factor — R²≈0 says the co-movement is regime, not factor,
and the hedge will be inert.

## arc_1074 — positive-skew CONTINUATION on the HONEST ENGINE (closes arc-1064's deferred engine test; the operator's ONE open in-charter thread)

**Why this arc (the specific gap).** The operator's 2026-06-06 LESSONS compression named ONE open
in-charter thread: positive-skew CONTINUATION — the corpus called trend-following dead using ONLY
+1R-capture and mean-forward-drift, win-rate lenses blind to a low-capture / fat-right-tail payoff.
The decisive prior is **arc 1064**, which ran the skew lens (MEAN + median + tail-removed) on the
textbook trend-continuation entry (Donchian break inside an SMA50/200 trend, both dirs) and KILLED it
— but **on GROSS `fwd_drift_atr`, explicitly NOT spending the engine**, on the argument *"gross drift
is generous → the SL-first engine is strictly worse → a gross cheap-kill suffices."* That bound is
**wrong in direction** for a take-the-loss trailing-runner exit: the −1R stop **caps** the gross
left-tail losers (−3..−5 ATR) that produced arc-1064's strongly-negative tail-removed gross mean, so
the honest-engine MEAN is *not* predictable from gross drift. The operator's redirection ("Scored
solely by MultiPairBacktester … trailing/run exits are the point") targets exactly this deferred run.

**What I did.** Re-expressed arc-1064's exact entry as a proper `SignalModule`
(`TrendContinuationBreakoutSignal`, dual-SMA trend + Donchian crossing-bar break, long AND short,
mid-OHLC shift1 — bar-for-bar matched to arc-1064 `build_obs`) and spent the honest
`ArcFoldRunner`→`A1Architecture`→`MultiPairBacktester` (FundedNext, risk 0.005) under the
positive-skew RUNNER exits ONLY (`sl_plus_trailing_atr`, `sl_plus_trailing_swing`,
`sl_partial_close_1r_runner_trail` × SL{1.5,2.0,2.5}, §5f nested walk-forward selection — no
tp_2r/3r, which cap the tail and defeat the premise). Judged by per-fold MEAN ROI + median-per-fold
ROI + per-trade R distribution + TAIL-REMOVED (+2R cap, drop-top-5%/fold, drop-top-K global) vs a
fair same-side random-entry null. Pre-registered the tail-luck≠skew kill-rule in the arc doc BEFORE
the run. IS 2010–2020, 8 evaluable folds (2013–2020); OOS NEVER touched.

**Result — KILL in all 4 cells, decisively (not marginal):**
- mean per-fold ROI −6.4% to −9.1%/yr; **mean per-trade R −0.42 to −0.70; median R ≈ −0.9** (a
  majority of trades take the −1R stop); **0/8 folds positive** in every cell.
- **No fat right tail to rescue it:** the largest single winner across the whole grid is +5.54R, and
  tail-removal (+2R cap; drop-top-5%/fold; drop-top-K{1,3,5} global) moves the mean by ≤0.9pp — it
  stays ≈−9%. This is the *opposite* of a skew edge: the mean is negative AND the tail is thin.
- §5f overwhelmingly selected `sl_plus_trailing_swing` at the TIGHTEST SL (1.5) — even the best
  honest runner exit cannot make the entry positive; the runner works (max +5.54R) but is fed a wall
  of −1R stops. Null: the two negative-est cells lose-to / barely-beat the fair null; the two
  "beats-null" cells are still −6%/−9%/yr → beats-null-but-net-negative = KILL (§11).
- Honest caveat: two OOS windows (2014, 2015) had ≈0 qualifying trend-breakouts and read 0.0% — the
  verdict rests on the **window-independent pooled per-trade R** (over 209–324 trades/cell), robust
  to that sparsity.

**The corrected lesson (new).** I hypothesized take-the-loss would LIFT arc-1064's negative gross
mean by capping the left tail. It does NOT. A Donchian-break-in-an-established-trend entry on liquid
FX majors is **adverse-first** — the classic false-breakout whipsaw: price pierces the channel, then
immediately retraces through the stop. So the −1R take-the-loss fires on the *majority* (median trade
≈ −0.9R), and the few dip-then-recover winners the gross lens credited are exactly the ones
take-the-loss kills. The honest engine is decisively negative *because of*, not despite, take-the-loss,
and there is no right tail fat enough to pay for the stop wall. **Methodological takeaway:** "gross
drift is strictly worse than the engine" is NOT a valid cheap-kill bound for a take-the-loss
trailing-runner exit on a continuation entry — the direction of the bias depends on path shape
(adverse-first vs favorable-first) and must be measured, not assumed. (For *reversion* entries with
favorable-first geometry the assumption holds; for *breakout/continuation* entries it inverts.)

**Meaning for the frontier.** Positive-skew continuation is now closed on BOTH lenses — gross
fwd-drift (arc 1064) AND the honest `MultiPairBacktester` under the correct positive-skew runner
exits (this arc). This was the operator's explicitly-flagged **one open in-charter thread**; it is now
closed by direct engine measurement rather than a proxy, removing the last "maybe the lens was wrong"
caveat from the within-charter terminus. Confirms arc-2000's "fat tail generic, not trend-selected"
on the explicit engine+skew axis, and arc-1064's gross verdict. Components UNCHANGED (all 4
PORTFOLIO; me_long-solo the honest deploy object; deployable count = 0). The standing levers are
unchanged and out-of-band: operator path-A gate-governance call and/or a charter unlock
(`NEEDS_ENABLEMENT.md` — note #1 cross-asset trend is the SAME positive-skew shape on a
less-efficient universe, where it is documented-fundable). No canonical change; no FLAG; no council
(decisive negative, not a survivor/fork). Reusable: `TrendContinuationBreakoutSignal` (any future
trend-continuation test) + the corrected gross-vs-engine bound caveat above.

## arc_1075 — positive-skew PULLBACK-RESUME continuation on the HONEST ENGINE (the last entry geometry; favorable-first hypothesis REFUTED)

**Disposition: KILL** (decisive engine negative; favorable-first geometry does NOT help). Full record
`discovery/arcs/arc_1075_pullback_resume_skew.md`; driver
`discovery/_disco1_work/arc1075_pullback_resume_skew.py`; new BUILT tool
`discovery/tools/trend_pullback_resume_signal.py` (`TrendPullbackResumeSignal`).

**Why (built on arc 1074's diagnosis).** Arc 1074 found the Donchian-breakout-in-trend continuation
entry decisively negative on the honest engine and diagnosed the cause as ADVERSE-FIRST geometry (you
buy the exact channel high; price retraces through the −1R stop on the majority before any runner can
develop). The mechanistic complement (DISCOVERY_DIRECTION S1 take-the-loss-tax geometry; `fbr` is its
reversion instance): enter the continuation AFTER the pullback, on the RESUMPTION bar, so the path is
FAVORABLE-FIRST and the −1R tax falls on noise trades not trend trades. This is the last continuation
entry GEOMETRY not yet run on the engine + positive-skew lens. Falsifiable: if "adverse-first" is the
cause, favorable-first should lift mean R toward 0/positive and grow a right tail; falsifier: if it is
still −R with no tail, the problem is not geometry — there is no continuation edge.

**Method.** New `TrendPullbackResumeSignal` (dual-SMA trend + a recent dip into the fast MA + a
resumption bar = close back above prior-bar high & fast MA; long AND short; ex-ante shift1). Same engine
machinery as arc 1074 — honest `ArcFoldRunner`→`A1Architecture`→`MultiPairBacktester`, FundedNext, risk
0.005, runner exits only (`sl_plus_trailing_atr`/`_swing`/partial-runner × SL{1.5,2,2.5}, §5f nested),
same pre-registered tail-luck≠skew guard + fair same-side null. IS 2010–2020, 8 evaluable folds; OOS
NEVER touched.

**Result — KILL in all 4 cells (long/short × sma{20/100 pb10, 50/200 pb15}, H4 USD majors):**
mean per-fold ROI −5.4 to −10.9%/yr; mean per-trade R −0.35 to −0.68; median R ≈ −0.78 to −0.90 (a
majority take the −1R stop); 0/8 folds positive; binding 2015/2018 negative; loses to the fair null in
3/4 cells (the one "beats null" cell is −11%/yr = beats-null-but-net-negative KILL).

**The hypothesis is REFUTED — and that is the value of the arc.** Favorable-first geometry did NOT help.
The long cells are actually WORSE than arc-1074's breakout (mean R −0.65/−0.68 vs −0.52) and have NO
right tail at all (the largest single winning position is ≈ 0R). Entering after the pullback does not
make the path favorable-first on liquid majors — the "resumption" immediately fails just as often as the
breakout. So "adverse-first" was a symptom, not the root cause. The root cause: **liquid-major price has
no exploitable post-trend continuation.** Whether you buy the breakout (1074) or the resumption (1075),
the next move is coin-flip-to-adverse, the −1R take-the-loss fires on the median trade, and no right tail
develops to pay for the stop wall. This is the conservation law (`frequency × edge ≈ const`, LESSONS
run-2) on the continuation axis: a trend-structural entry samples the near-martingale, so it is a
coin-flip net of cost — and take-the-loss + a runner exit cannot manufacture skew from a martingale.

**Frontier status.** Combined with arc 1074 (Donchian breakout edge), arc 2081 (continuation book +
shock re-measured under trailing), and arc 2082 (vol-expansion breakout) — all KILL under the
operator-mandated mean + median-per-fold + tail-removed lens on the honest engine — **positive-skew
continuation is now airtight-closed across every entry geometry** (breakout-edge, vol-expansion, shock,
continuation-book, favorable-first pullback-resume). This was the operator's ONE open in-charter thread
(LESSONS 2026-06-06); it is comprehensively closed by direct engine measurement under the mandated
metric. The in-charter frontier returns to the convergent terminus: 0 PASS, 4 PORTFOLIO, deployable=0;
levers remain out-of-band (operator path-A gate-governance call and/or a charter unlock —
`NEEDS_ENABLEMENT.md` #1 cross-asset trend is the SAME positive-skew shape on a less-efficient universe,
where it is documented-fundable; the in-charter FX version is what these arcs just closed). Components
UNCHANGED; no canonical change; no FLAG; no council (decisive negative, not a survivor/fork). Reusable:
`TrendPullbackResumeSignal` + the refuted-favorable-first lesson (continuation failure on liquid majors
is edge-absence, not entry-geometry).

## arc_2084 — Positive-skew trend continuation on the DAILY timeframe (the last un-varied axis: TF, not entry geometry)

Full record: [`arcs/arc_2084_d1_trend_continuation_skew.md`](arcs/arc_2084_d1_trend_continuation_skew.md).

1074/2081, vol-expansion 2082, pullback-resume 1075/2083, shock 2081) — but **every one ran on H4.** The
single axis none varied is the **sampling timeframe**, and for THIS payoff shape that is not cosmetic. The
classic positive-skew trend edge (Turtle: 20/55-day Donchian, 2N stop) is a DAILY phenomenon *because* a
take-the-loss trailing stop's whipsaw rate = (stop width)/(intra-trend pullback size): on H4 the 2·ATR(H4)
stop is hit by intra-trend noise (arc 2081 median trade −0.81R, winner can't run); on D1 the stop sits
~√6× wider relative to the trend, the mechanistic hope being it survives ordinary pullbacks and lets the
fat tail develop. Never run on the honest engine under the mandated lens.

**What I did.** arc 1074's EXACT harness, sole change H4→**D1 + full 28-pair universe** (timeframe as the
only varied axis): `TrendContinuationBreakoutSignal` dual-SMA 50/200 × Donchian {20,55} × {long,short},
trailing exits × SL{1.5,2,2.5}, §5f nested exit/SL selection, the pre-registered tail-removed guard
(G1 mean / G2 +2R-cap+top-5%+drop-top-K / G3 median-per-fold), same-side random null.

**Result — all 4 cells KILL at IS; OOS preserved.** mean ROI −0.88 to −4.29%/yr; mean per-trade R −0.04
to −0.17; **median trade R −0.84 to −0.94 (the −1R stop-wall is INTACT on D1)**; tail-removal worsens
every cell; folds-positive 1–3/8. Two findings:

1. **Timeframe IS a real geometry lever (directionally borne out).** D1 bleeds ~8× LESS than H4 —
   Turtle-long-D55 −0.88%/yr vs the H4 continuation book's −6 to −22%/yr (1074/2081); per-trade mean R
   improves −0.13R (H4) → −0.043R (D1). The mechanistic prediction (slower ⇒ wider stop ⇒ less whipsaw)
   is partially confirmed: per-loss size shrinks. And the Turtle-long does the long-vol thing the thread
   sought — **+10.09% in 2015** (the reversion book's death year) and it **beats the being-in-vol null by
   +3.16pp** (the daily-trend ENTRY adds positive value, unlike on H4 where entry ≈ random/worse).

2. **…but it is NOT a sign lever (decisive).** The median trade is still a −1R stop on D1 — the breakout
   is **adverse-first even at daily resolution** (resumes often enough to fire, pulls back through the stop
   before the tail develops). The mean never crosses zero, the right tail (max +4.5–7.9R) is generic and
   insufficient, tail-removal worsens every cell. The one beats-null cell (Turtle-long-D55) is still
   **net-negative** ⇒ **KILL, not PORTFOLIO** (§11: beats-null-but-net-negative; can't diversify a
   negative-mean component positive). Conservation law on the timeframe axis: slowing the clock moves the
   loss geometry without flipping the sign.

**Closure.** With the H4 arcs, positive-skew continuation is now closed across **entry geometry AND
timeframe** on liquid-FX OHLC. The genuine long-vol / positive-skew diversifier the vehicle wall needs
lives in a **less-efficient instrument universe** (cross-asset trend, NEEDS_ENABLEMENT #1; same shape,
blocker = historical data) — confirming the Run-2 council's structural placement. Residual (low EV): W1 is
the only finer-grained TF cell left, but the D1→H4 gradient (bleed shrinks, sign fixed, median −1R) + W1

   was the only offset to a wall of small −1R losers). Textbook thin-tail trap (cf. 2082 +132R, 1077 +18R).

   stop" entry pays the spread on a small absolute move = the worst cost-to-edge ratio; the full 28-pair
   universe is −17 to −21%/yr vs USD7's −4 to −10% (arc 1003's cross-cost amplification). Only 1/8 cells
   beats the null (USD7 coil20-long +2.68pp) and it is net −5.46% ⇒ beats-null-but-net-negative = KILL (§11).

gross kill (1062) and the honest-engine kill **AGREE, and the engine is even MORE decisive.** The reason
clarifies the 1074 corrected bound: 1074's continuation entry had a modest gross left tail the stop could
cap; the compression breakout is *adverse-first with no compensating right tail at all* (largest long winner

right to offset it. A no-right-tail adverse-first entry is therefore killed *harder* by the honest engine,
not rescued — exactly what the corrected 1074 bound ("gross-vs-engine bias direction depends on path shape")
predicts. So: the squeeze / volatility-contraction-breakout / small-stop premise is **empirically false on
liquid FX** — the tight stop amplifies cost, not skew, because the break doesn't run.
